body:
## Summary

Two long-standing problems with Table column resizing:

1. **The divider was drawn 8px left of the column boundary.** The handle was a flex child of the header cell with `margin -4px` on both sides, so it sat at the end of the cell's content box, inside the cell's horizontal padding (`sm`, 8px). `ColumnResizePrimitive` paints its line at the handle center, so every divider line appeared 8px inside the cell, and grabbing the visible cell edge missed the handle.
2. **The last column could not be resized.** `table_column_model` excluded it (`index + 1 < len`), so it had no handle.

This PR positions the handle absolutely, so cell padding cannot shift it:

- Column *i*'s handle lives at the left edge of header cell *i + 1* (`left: -4px`). It paints after cell *i*, so the half that reaches into cell *i* is drawn and hit-tested on top of it.
- The last column's handle sits at the right edge of its own cell (`right: 0`). Widening the last column scrolls the table horizontally, because the root already scrolls on x.
- Header refs are declared once per render, because a handle now measures the previous cell through that cell's ref.

## Evidence

Real app: oh-my-byted, a 9-column resizable Table on gpui-rhai 0.1.7 with the same diff applied. Geometry comes from the accessibility snapshot (`columnheader` vs `separator` bounds).

| | handles | handle center − header right edge |
|---|---|---|
| before | 8 (no last column) | −8px for all 8 |
| after | 9 | 0px for the 8 inner columns; the last handle ends exactly at the header's right edge |

## Regression tests

- `tests/native-keyboard` adds `table_resize_handles_sit_on_column_boundaries_including_the_last_column`. It mounts a three-column resizable Table and asserts:
  - each inner handle's center sits on the column boundary (±0.5px);
  - the last column's handle ends at the header's right edge;
  - a real mouse drag starting **2px right of** a boundary (over the next header cell) widens the left column by 40px;
  - a drag on the last column's handle widens that column by 40px.

  Without the fix it fails with `Name: handle center 113 must sit on the column boundary 121`.
- `official_registry.rs` is updated:
  - every column of a resizable table now carries a width signal and autofit measures;
  - new `assert_table_resize_handles` checks where each handle lives (cell *i* holds column *i − 1*'s handle with `left: -4px`; the last cell also holds its own with `right: 0`) and its accessible label.

## Checks run locally (on this branch)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (root and `tests/native-keyboard`)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` (root and `tests/native-keyboard`)
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`: 603 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --manifest-path tests/performance/Cargo.toml --locked`: 2 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --manifest-path tests/native-keyboard/Cargo.toml --locked`: 134 passed, 0 failed
- `bash scripts/audit-visual-baselines.sh`: passed (69 PNG files)

## Needs a recapture

`examples/data_table` uses `resizable_columns: true`, so the `tests/visual/macos/data_table/*.png` baselines will drift:

- the divider lines move 8px right, onto the cell edges;
- the last column gains a divider at the table's right edge.

I can't recapture them here because this machine has no screen recording permission. The audit only checks the files, so it still passes.

## Behavior notes

- A press within 4px right of a boundary now starts a resize instead of reaching the next header cell (for example, its sort click). That is the expected hit area for a divider.
- Dragging a flex last column converts it to a fixed width, the same as for any other column. Narrowing it leaves empty space on the right.
- CHANGELOG is not touched; release PRs seem to write it.

title: fix(table): put column resize handles on the boundary, include the last column
